title: U.S. House · California's 49th District
area: North coastal San Diego County and southern Orange County, including San Clemente, Oceanside, Carlsbad and San Juan Capistrano.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, a mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved on November 5, 2025.

Incumbent Mike Levin and Armen Kurdian advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating Star Parker. Levin won 55.9% of the primary vote (125,869 votes) and Kurdian won 26.1% (58,822 votes); Parker received 18.0%.

candidates.name: Mike Levin
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 55.9% of the vote.

summary.text: Mike Levin is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 49th District, first elected in 2018. An environmental attorney before Congress, he now serves on the House Appropriations Committee. His official biography highlights clean energy, veterans' issues and the decommissioning of the San Onofre nuclear plant.

background.text: According to his official biography, he was raised in South Orange County and attended Loyola High School in Los Angeles.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Stanford University in 2001, where his official biography says he was student body president, and a J.D. from Duke University School of Law in 2005. He was also a Coro Fellow.
Worked as an attorney specializing in environmental and energy regulatory compliance and governmental affairs, and as an environmental attorney before Congress.
Served as executive director of the Democratic Party of Orange County, served on the board of the Center for Sustainable Energy and, according to his official biography, co-founded Sustain OC.
Won the open 49th District seat in November 2018, defeating Republican Diane Harkey 56.4% to 43.6%, and was re-elected in 2020.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he serves on the House Appropriations Committee, on its Energy and Water Development and Military Construction, Veterans Affairs subcommittees. Earlier he chaired the Veterans' Affairs Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity (2021-2022) and was its ranking member (2023-2024).

His official biography says more than 32 of his bills have been signed into law, including the Johnny Isakson and David P. Roe, M.D. Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act of 2020, and that he founded and co-chairs the Spent Nuclear Fuel Solutions Caucus.

According to his official biography, he is a member of the New Democrat Coalition, the Congressional Progressive Caucus and the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, and lives in San Juan Capistrano with his wife and two children.

priorities.text: Building clean energy and lowering energy costs, including by opposing termination of federal clean-energy grants in the district.
Protecting Southern California's coastline from new offshore oil and gas drilling.
priorities.quote: I am proud to represent 50 miles of beautiful Southern California coastline and the vibrant coastal economy that relies on its clean and healthy ocean ecosystem.

positions.summary: Pushed the Interior Department to end delays and procedural hurdles blocking wind and solar energy project permits, saying the Trump administration has been disadvantaging renewable projects while favoring fossil energy.
positions.quote: We write to request an update on the status of clean energy projects that the Department of the Interior (DOI) has been delaying arbitrarily.

positions.summary: Joined medical providers and patients in demanding that Congress halt proposals to cut Medicaid funding.
positions.quote: We don’t have to guess what happens when Medicaid funding is slashed. We’ve seen it before.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations for the 119th Congress (2025-2026), including the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies subcommittee and the Military Construction, Veterans Affairs and Related Agencies subcommittee.

Chaired the Economic Opportunity Subcommittee of the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs during the 117th Congress (2021-2022) and served as ranking member of that subcommittee in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

Led a letter with House colleagues to the Department of Energy in August 2026 condemning the termination of 321 clean-energy grants, including projects in the 49th District, and demanding their reinstatement.

candidates.researchNotes: Levin has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and his official website's /issues page has no per-topic issue statements; positions and priorities here are drawn from his official press releases on clean energy and offshore drilling.

candidates.name: Armen Kurdian
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 26.1% of the vote, defeating fellow Republican Star Parker.

summary.text: Armen Kurdian is a retired U.S. Navy captain with more than 25 years of service running as the Republican candidate for CA-49. He has not previously held elected office. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes his service as leading large civilian, military and union organizations, and says he has volunteered in local nonprofits and local government.

background.text: Attended Wichita East High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Kansas in 1993.
Served in the U.S. Navy from 1993 to 2018 and retired as a captain; says he led large organizations of hundreds of people, including civil, military and union workforces.
Earned a graduate degree from the Naval Postgraduate School in 2003 and another from Cornell University in 2014.
Lists engineering manager as his career experience.
Says that after retiring he continued community service in local nonprofits and local government, and that he has volunteered thousands of hours without payment.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 26.1% of the vote, behind Levin (55.9%).

priorities.text: Reducing the cost of living, saying it is his top priority and citing residents leaving California over costs and job losses.
Improving public schools by focusing on core curriculum and vocational/trades training rather than what he calls polarizing social issues.
Rebuilding California's manufacturing and shipbuilding industries by working with business and labor.

candidates.researchNotes: Based on his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website content could be retrieved.

statements.quote: Schools are failing our kids, especially those of lower income who are unable to attend private or alternative schools.
